title: SRE weekly stability briefing + handoff notes — 2027-02-03
content:
TL;DR
- Week of 2027-01-28 to 2027-02-03. Overall platform availability stable but we hit two production incidents that impacted request latency and one minor routing flake. No customer-facing data exposure.
- Action items prioritized: kernel probe rollback (short-term), autoscale policy tweak for region eu-west-1 (mid-term), and runbook clarity on prefix-caching fallback (ongoing).

Incidents (summary)
1) High tail latency — 2027-01-30 03:12 UTC (sev-2)
- Symptom: 95th/99th latency spikes for text-gen API in eu-west-1 for ~22 minutes.
- Root cause hypothesis: degraded NVMe I/O on a subset of dedicated hosts causing degraded KV cache eviction behavior and longer cold-starts for attention KV.
- Mitigation: automated fallback routing to spare dedicated pool; temporary increase in batching cap to reduce per-token overhead for affected requests.
- Post-incident: rolled back last kernel change on affected nodes; follow-up investigation ticket SRE-1423 (storage-health and kernel-probe rollback).

2) Model shard routing mismatch — 2027-01-31 14:41 UTC (sev-3)
- Symptom: ~0.6% of requests returned model-incompatible error when cross-region fallback triggered.
- Root cause: mismatch between model variant tags in routing table and the compiled model artifact metadata after last deployment.
- Mitigation: hotfix to routing service to validate artifact signatures at routing time; queued longer-term fix to add artifact-tag checks during deployment.
- Post-incident: added unit test and a small schema validation PR (see linked PR).

3) Internal alert storm (no customer impact) — 2027-02-02 09:05 UTC (informational)
- Symptom: surge of duplicate alerts for autoscale policy flips during a short traffic surge from internal load tests.
- Root cause: double-notify bug in autoscaler reconciliation loop when metrics arrive in burst.
- Mitigation: rate-limited alert aggregator deployed; bug ticket SRE-1430.

SLO snapshot (rolling 7d)
- Text generation availability: 99.92% (target 99.9%) — passing but fragile in eu-west-1.
- Embeddings latency p50/p95: 42ms / 110ms (target p95 < 120ms) — healthy.
- Dedicated pool capacity utilization (global average): 74% (peak 94% in eu-west-1 during incident window).
- Error budget burn: small positive balance for monthly window; monitor daily.

On-call handoff (morning) — key bullets for next shift
- Current open pages: SRE-1423 (kernel probe rollback / storage health), SRE-1430 (autoscaler alert storm), ROUTE-559 (model artifact-tagging mismatch).
- Immediate priorities: monitor eu-west-1 KV cache hit ratio and latencies; validate rollback continues to hold during primetime traffic.
- If latency > p95 threshold for >10m: escalate to runtime-oncall and initiate controlled routing blue->green for affected pools.
- If autoscaler starts flipping frequently: disable burst autoscale, enable manual scaling for the next 2 hours, and notify platform-eng.
- Handoff checklist: confirm runbook version (v2.1) open, update incident channel with brief summary, confirm escalation contacts for runtime-oncall and infra-oncall.

Runbook & docs updates
- Added a short section "KV cache eviction symptoms & mitigation" to runbook v2.1 — includes diagnostic queries and safe rollback steps.
- Marked deployment pipeline stage 'artifact-tag-validation' as required for canary -> prod promotion.
- Note: runbook still needs a step for NVMe SMART check automation (owner: Jon Park, due 2027-02-10).

Action items and owners
- Maya Chen: complete kernel probe rollback postmortem write-up (SRE-1423) — due 2027-02-06.
- Ravi Patel: implement autoscaler alert de-dup logic and unit tests (SRE-1430) — due 2027-02-08.
- Elena Korov: add artifact signature validation to routing service and open API contract doc — due 2027-02-14.
- Jon Park: prototype NVMe SMART automation script and add to infra runbook — due 2027-02-10.

Operational notes / metrics to watch this week
- eu-west-1 dedicated pool: KV cache hit ratio (target > 87%), 95th token latency, NVMe I/O wait stats.
- Autoscaler flip rate (count per hour) and alert noise metric.
- Model artifact deploy success rate and routing validation failures.

Meeting and syncs
- Weekly SRE triage: Tuesday 2027-02-02, 10:30 PST — attendees: eng-sre, runtime, infra. Quick decisions captured above.
- Runbook review sync scheduled Friday 2027-02-05, 16:00 CET — agenda: SMART automation, artifact validation, postmortem outline.

Open questions / risks
- Risk: repeated NVMe degradation in a small subset of hosts may signal hardware fleet aging — need to decide if we should accelerate replacement cadence for the affected racks.
- Question: should we default to warming a small cross-region spare pool for models with high tail-sensitivity? pros/cons list in weekly meeting notes.

Notes to self / scratchpad
- Try running synthetic requests with long-context tokens to reproduce KV eviction pattern.
- Check storage node SMART logs for 2027-01-29..2027-02-01.

Appendix (links and quick refs)
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-1423
- Autoscale bug: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-1430
- Routing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/876
- Runbook v2.1: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/Runbooks

End of brief.
